findings.title: Deleting the cache doesn't refetch connectedCalendars, so the old "Last updated" stays on screen
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()`. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (lines 61-64), it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377` renders `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` without `onChanged`, and the wrapper's query sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` (`SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:152-161`). So on the event-type Advanced tab, the user sees "Cache deleted successfully" while the dropdown still shows "Cache Status / Last updated: <old time>" and "Delete cached data" until they reload. Add an `onSettled` that awaits `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: Error-state calendars can no longer be removed when `disableConnectionModification` is set
findings.body: Before this change, the Alert branch (calendar with no listable calendars, i.e. a broken credential) only checked `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId` before showing the remove button. It ignored `disableConnectionModification`. Now `CredentialActionsDropdown` applies `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification` (`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68`). On the event-type Advanced tab (`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375` passes `true`), a broken credential used to have a remove action and now has none. If that's intended, note it in the PR description. Otherwise pass `disableConnectionModification` only from the first branch.

findings.title: Does `updateMany` with empty `data` actually bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`?
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma setting the `@updatedAt` field (`schema.prisma:860`) automatically. As far as I know, Prisma's engine only adds `@updatedAt` when the write args are non-empty, and treats an empty update as a no-op. If so, this line writes nothing. Also, nothing in the PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`: the UI shows `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly, or drop the call along with the unused `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` additions in `user.ts:899-900` and `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28`. Right now each webhook-triggered refresh adds a DB round trip.

findings.title: A missing or foreign credential returns 500 instead of a tRPC NOT_FOUND
findings.body: `throw new Error(...)` surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and gets reported as a server failure. Other tRPC handlers use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) for ownership checks. The client shows a generic toast either way, so only error reporting and status codes are affected.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the "en-US" locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale, while the surrounding label is translated through `t()`. A user with a non-US locale sees an M/D/YY date inside a translated sentence, and day/month order is ambiguous for them. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) instead.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is BSD-only, and `ENV_FILE` depends on the current directory
findings.body: On GNU sed (Linux), `sed -i '' -E ...` treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env file is never updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved from the caller's current directory, not the script's location. Run from the repo root, it creates or edits a `.env` outside the repository. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")`, and write the file in a portable way (e.g. a temp file plus `mv`). Also, `cleanup` exits 0 on the failure paths (lines 49, 57), which hides the failure from callers.

findings.title: Existing cache rows will show the migration time as "Last updated"
findings.body: `DEFAULT NOW()` fills every existing `CalendarCache` row with the deploy time. Until a webhook refreshes it, the new dropdown shows that time as the cache's last update, even though the cached data may be much older. The header comment still says the column is added "without a default value", which is no longer true.

contracts.action: User confirms "Delete cached data" in the credential dropdown
contracts.equivalent_path: disconnectMutation in the same file / DisconnectIntegration mutation
contracts.before_after: The disconnect path invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations in onSettled (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:61-64, DisconnectIntegration.tsx:36-39). deleteCache only calls the optional onSuccess prop.
contracts.visible_effect: Shows a toast. The list only refreshes if the parent passes onChanged: CalendarListContainer does (CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88, 113), EventAdvancedTab doesn't (EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-377), so the old timestamp stays there.
contracts.failure_mode: onError shows the error_deleting_cache toast. The dialog is already closed (line 137). Nothing else changes state.

contracts.action: deleteCache handler deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.before_after: Checks ownership with findFirst({id, userId}) right before the delete. The deleteMany is scoped to that credentialId, and the cache is regenerated from Google on the next fetch or webhook.
contracts.visible_effect: Returns success:true. Availability falls back to live Google requests until the cache is repopulated.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing credential throws a plain Error (500). A deleteMany failure propagates to the client toast. No journal is involved.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars attaches cacheUpdatedAt via a groupBy on CalendarCache
contracts.before_after: Runs after getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb. It always uses the real repository (not the feature-flag mock) and includes expired rows.
contracts.visible_effect: CredentialActionsDropdown shows cache status for Google credentials with a non-null cacheUpdatedAt.
contracts.failure_mode: A groupBy failure fails the entire connectedCalendars query, so the calendars settings list breaks.

contracts.action: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache bumps SelectedCalendar updatedAt with empty data
contracts.failure_mode: If it throws, the webhook handler fails after the cache has already been written.
contracts.open_question: Does Prisma updateMany with empty data actually set @updatedAt?

summary: This PR adds a cache status / delete-cache action to a new credential dropdown, a CalendarCache.updatedAt column, and a tunnelmole dev script. The delete path checks credential ownership right before deleting. The main defect: deleting the cache doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars, so the old timestamp stays visible wherever the parent passes no onChanged (the event-type Advanced tab). Smaller points: broken credentials can no longer be removed when disableConnectionModification is set; the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump with empty data is probably a no-op and nothing reads it; the delete handler throws a plain Error (500); the timestamp is always formatted as en-US; and the shell script only works on macOS and resolves .env from the caller's current directory.
